subject: Urgent: customer stream hangs during spike — proxy buffering suspected (SLA risk)
messages:

Subject: Live transcription stream hung during 09:00 PST spike

Hi David —

We started seeing a steady stream of partial / silent responses in our real-time transcription during the 09:00 PST traffic spike. Clients report the socket stays open but we stop receiving chunks for ~6–8s, then the server side eventually closes with a 504. This pattern started after your 2027-05-20 infra kernel update on the hosted cluster (us-west-2).

Impact: ~7% increase in error rate for streaming endpoints; throughput down ~15% for our highest-concurrency routes. This is blocking our launch next week.

Attached: session-trace-20270523.json (contains session id: s-81c4ae), a small client-side tcpdump, and a short reproduction script.

Can you confirm receipt and advise immediate mitigation?

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: david.kim@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@triagehealth.com
Date: 2027-05-23T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live transcription stream hung during 09:00 PST spike

Quick triage notes (internal):

Observed:  us-west-2 live-routing cluster shows elevated ‘chunk_gap’ metric starting 2027-05-20 03:00 UTC. Nginx upstream logs show repeated "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)" while the backend runtime still reports active KV-cache and no OOM.

Hypothesis: intermediate proxy (FastFront or an internal edge) is buffering chunked responses until a full chunk or until connection idle timer expires, then returning a 504/connection reset. WebSocket PING/PONG look healthy from backend -> client, but we see no client-ack logs.

Steps taken:
- Pulled session s-81c4ae: we can see a sequence of tiny chunks (<128B) followed by silence and then connection termination.
- Collected nginx-upstream-snippet.log from the affected nodes and attached it.

Initial mitigations to try ASAP:
1) Disable proxy_response_buffering on FastFront for the affected route (if supported) to allow chunk flush-through.
2) Reduce keepalive timeouts and increase worker_connections on the proxy to avoid half-open buffering.
3) If mitigation not possible quickly, move TriageHealth to a Dedicated pool in us-west-2 (actionable now).

Requesting:
- Markus: quick check if there are runtime kernel-level networking changes from 2027-05-20 that might affect socket TCP windowing or Nagle behavior.
- David: can we authorize emergency routing to Dedicated (customer is high-tier, DEAL-4781)?

— Vanessa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: nginx-upstream-snippet.log (text/plain)

We're under a hard launch deadline next week and the error/throughput regression is material to our UX. If rolling to Dedicated removes the risk quickly we want that path. Also: our SRE asked to be on the exec call if credits / SLA exceptions are discussed.

— Elaine

From: david.kim@redwood.ai

Cc: sales-leads@redwood.ai, account-exec@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-24T12:00:00-07:00
Subject: Exec ask — TriageHealth live-stream degradation (DEAL-4781)

Executive summary for leadership:
- Impact: TriageHealth (enterprise customer, launch next week) is experiencing streaming chunk starvation leading to transient silent frames and 504s. Observed +7% streaming error rate and -18% throughput on their routes during spikes.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): FastFront CDN recently enabled micro-chunk consolidation -> proxy buffering interacting with our chunked transfer path. Secondary contributor: our kernel/networking changes from 2027-05-20 may have increased susceptibility to small-chunk flows.
- Immediate mitigations: disable proxy buffering on FastFront, route customer to Dedicated pool (fast), or apply a quick runtime change to force larger chunk coalescing at source (needs rollout).
- Ask: Approval to (A) spin up a Dedicated pool for TriageHealth for the next 72 hours (cost covered by Redwood while we root cause); (B) pre-authorize a customer credit of up to 25% for the impacted billing period if mitigation isn't timely; (C) schedule an 08:00 PST exec sync tomorrow with SRE and sales to confirm customer comms.

Please reply with Y/N and any follow-ups. I'll prepare the incident bridge notes and a short customer-facing status if we get approval.

— David Kim
Head of Customer Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: david.kim@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@triagehealth.com
Date: 2027-05-25T07:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec ask — TriageHealth live-stream degradation (DEAL-4781)

Update after deeper infra review and FastFront coordination:

Findings:
- FastFront confirmed FF-992 (micro-chunk consolidation) and documented that they will buffer chunked responses until either the chunk buffer hits 512B or their flush interval expires. In high-concurrency bursts this created a head-of-line delay where many tiny chunks were held, leading to upstream timeouts.
- Our runtime change on 2027-05-20 adjusted the token emission path to emit many smaller micro-chunks (<128B) to reduce latency under normal conditions. That combination exposed the buffering behavior.

Mitigation performed (rolled out 07:00 UTC):
1) Requested FastFront to disable micro-chunk consolidation on the specific route -> immediate reduction in chunk_gap metrics on the observed nodes.
2) Rolled back the smallest-chunk emission heuristic on the affected model-serving pool (hotfix rolled to canary then to 40% of traffic).
3) Temporary routing: moved TriageHealth to a Dedicated pool while we validate stability and iterate on a long-term fix.

Proposed follow-ups:
- Runbook addition: check for FastFront/edge buffering settings when we see chunk_gap anomalies.
- Postmortem to include timeline, code changes (token emission heuristic), and recommendations for model-serving defaults to avoid micro-chunk emission under proxy-buffering networks.
- Customer compensation recommendation: 20% credit for affected billing window and commitment to a runbook review.

cc: ops@triagehealth.com — please confirm that your side sees a stable feed after the routing change; we'll keep the Dedicated route for 72 hours by default.

— Markus Klein
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mitigation-checklist-20270525.md (text/markdown)
